title: Skinny Johnson, the Johnson brothers and Joe Steele's arranging
summary: Waters calls Skinny Johnson one of the greatest pianists he ever heard, names the Johnson brothers, and says Steele's arrangements were crowded, unlike Sy Oliver's, a contrast he links to Wilcox.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It's only one job that I can remember that I could take courses and was on a jazz gig, was Skinny Johnson. That was a guy who I'll always say that was actually one of the greatest piano players I ever heard, I mean it's a shame that he wasn't known. He was a -
Skinny Johnson, he's no relation to Bobby. You know Bobby Johnson, don't you?
And Howard, they're brothers, you know.
Yeah. Bobby the guitarist and Howard the -

And he had another brother, played piano called Walter Johnson. Now Walter, he was a, Walter Johnson was like this piano player, more society type, you know. Very musical, and he played by himself. He played at, in -
high class hotels, you know. Technic - fantastic. Now -
Joe Steele, by the way, is the same Joe Steele who later played with Chick Webb -

That's the one, that worked with Chick Webb, see, exactly. And he - some people say he played too much piano, you know, some people said. But that's from his knowledge up there in the school where he studied. And used to arrange, and they said the same thing about his arrangements, said 'Too crowded', you know, the arranging. If you have a tendency to make a lot of notes when you play, you're taught, the arranger - you do the same thing. See, that's the difference between, the same point - this is like Sy Oliver and Wilcox. Wilcox was a pianist, you know, so he, when Wilcox made arrangements - man, those notes was comin' out from all kinds of ways, they's hard as hell to play, you know. But Sy, when he made an arrangement, it was swingin' - he had a few notes, and every note meant something, and it still does, you see. It's still that you, I find that. I even had that same tendency when I used to first 'range, to make too many notes. Well, I corrected that by listening to other guys, you know. So I could, that's why I could arrange pretty well.
